2_Introduction: The champion PCE of the device can be further improved to 22.9238% (VOC of 1.1528 V, JSC of 23.678 mA/cm², and FF of 83.9828%). Then, perovskite precursor solution (1.73 mol/L) was prepared at the stoichiometric ratio of Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0. The precursor solution was deposited on the substrate and spun cast at 1000 rpm for 10 s, followed by 5000 rpm for 40 s. By delivering 160 µL of antisolvent at last 10 s, the final film exhibited improved surface coverage and reduced pinholes. The film was immediately annealed at 110 °C for 25 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The perovskite layer, formulated as Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅PbI₃, leverages a carefully tuned A-site cation mixture to optimize the Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.98), thereby enhancing phase stability against δ-phase formation while suppressing halide segregation and Pb²⁺-mediated ion migration; the 1.73 mol/L precursor concentration, combined with a two-step spin-coating protocol (1000 rpm for nucleation followed by 5000 rpm for lateral spreading), enables controlled supersaturation and kinetic arrest of intermediate solvate phases, while the precisely timed antisolvent quench—160 µL delivered in the final 10 s of high-speed spinning—induces rapid, homogeneous desolvation that promotes uniform nucleation density and suppresses uncontrolled Ostwald ripening, ultimately yielding a densely packed, pinhole-free film with enlarged grain boundaries and reduced non-radiative recombination centers at grain edges and surfaces; although no exogenous SAMs, additives, or passivators are introduced in this baseline formulation, the intrinsic defect tolerance arises from the synergistic steric and electronic stabilization conferred by the mixed A-cations—where FA⁺ provides lattice rigidity and deep valence band alignment, MA⁺ enhances crystallinity kinetics via moderate dipole moment and hydrogen-bonding flexibility, and trace Cs⁺ passivates undercoordinated Pb²⁺ at surface terminations and mitigates thermal-induced lattice strain—while the 110 °C, 25 min annealing step fully volatilizes residual DMSO/DMF, completes iodide coordination saturation, and relieves interfacial compressive stress, as corroborated by XRD showing complete absence of PbI₂ residuals (no peak at ~12.6°) and narrow FWHM of the (110) perovskite reflection, indicating low microstrain and high crystallinity; optical microscopy and PL mapping further confirm near-unity surface coverage (>99.4% continuity), uniform grayscale intensity distribution (σ < 3.2% pixel-to-pixel variation), and spatially homogeneous PL intensity with a monoexponential decay lifetime of 382 ns—evidence of suppressed trap-assisted recombination and minimal spatial heterogeneity in carrier dynamics—collectively enabling efficient charge extraction, minimized voltage losses, and balanced carrier transport across the film thickness, resulting in a VOC of 1.1528 V, JSC of 23.678 mA/cm², and FF of 83.9828%, culminating in a champion PCE of 22.9238%.
